---
title: "Companion curriculum"
subtitle: "The teaching modules of the EU-frames case"
---

The course is built around one exercise: you reproduce a recorded result, vary the analysis behind it, declare one analysis before you run it, and read your result against those of the class. On this site the exercise is taught on the EU-frames case, a panel of 270 country-years built from sixteen Eurobarometer waves, on which a published claim links the economic performance of a country to the terms in which its citizens frame the European Union, and the [case study](../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd) tells it in full. A single day has room for that exercise and little else, so the skills around it are taught in these fifteen modules, which run from R and the IDE to a reanalysis that you can deposit and register. Each module stands on its own, so you can take the one you need and leave the rest.

Every module is written for this case. The modules that run code compute their numbers from the files of the case in `cases/eu-frames/data/` when the page is built, so that a module can be read as a worked analysis as well as an explanation, and you can check each number against your own output. The models that need the respondents themselves, whose Eurobarometer files may not be passed on, were fitted once on the licensed files, and the modules display the saved output of those models beside the code that produced it.

Nothing here is required for the one-day workshop, which runs in full without any module and with no account to create. Its pages point at some modules as preparation, at others as the slower companion of a part of the day, and at the rest as reading for afterwards. The [Extended course](../tracks/eu-frames-extended/index.qmd) teaches some of them as the sessions of its first and third days, and the [self-study track](../tracks/self-study/index.qmd) reads the modules in its stages, between the tasks of the case.

The modules fall into the three groups of the Companion menu. The first holds the computational tools with which an analysis is written, the second the data and the public records that let others find an analysis and run it again, and the third the statistical methods with which the case is analysed. Within each group the order is roughly the order of what each module assumes.

## Tools {#sec-tools}

The modules on the tools are on the umbrella site of the course, written once for the four cases on the data of the housing-audit case: [Getting started with R](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/r.html) with its [second part](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/r-further.html), [Positron and other IDEs](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/ide.html), [Quarto documents](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/quarto.html) and [Git and GitHub](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/git-github.html), and the [setup page](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html) of the same site installs R, Quarto, an IDE and the workspace, with the [setup help](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/help.html) beside it. Two modules of this site take the same tools to the panel and the workspace of the EU-frames case:

- [R on the country-year panel](intro-r.qmd) – the files of the case and the routes by which they arrive, the grammar of graphics on the panel of the case, and reading its specification curve.
- [The workspace in the IDE](ide.qmd) – six steps through the workspace of the case, in whichever IDE you chose.

## Data and sharing {#sec-sharing}

- [Social science data sources](data-sources.qmd) – the three routes by which data reach a researcher, a map of the archives and series, and the routes of the case from GESIS, the World Bank, Eurostat and the OSF.
- [Building the analysis file](data-management.qmd) – the steps of a build, worked through for the country-year panel of the case from the sixteen Eurobarometer waves and checked against the committed files.
- [Reproducibility repositories](repositories.qmd) – what a repository does, the SCORE dossier and the Multi100 records of the paper, the OSF after 2026, registrations, and depositing a reanalysis of your own.

## Methods {#sec-methods}

- [Panel data](panel-data.qmd) – the estimators of the country-year panel: the linear model, clustered standard errors with few clusters, the two fixed-effects designs, random effects and the within–between model.
- [Multilevel models](multilevel.qmd) – respondents in country-years in countries, in the vocabularies of four disciplines: random intercepts and slopes, the published model, two designs, survey weights, bounded outcomes and the education gap.
- [Binary outcomes](binary-outcomes.qmd) – one survey item as a yes-or-no outcome: logit and probit, errors clustered by country-year, average marginal effects, the national unemployment rate and a random intercept.
- [Causal graphs and adjustment sets](dags.qmd) – what a causal graph commits you to, confounders, mediators and colliders, the graph of the case and its adjustment set, and what fixed effects cannot absorb.
- [The items behind the scales](measurement.qmd) – the thirteen items behind every outcome of the menu, how they hang together, their factor structure and reliability, and the outcome decisions of the curve.
- [Weights](weighting.qmd) – survey weights within a cell, precision weights across cells and population weights across countries, which of them changes the estimand, and weights in estimation.
- [Missing answers](missingness.qmd) – the respondent who mentions no frame, the three mechanisms of missingness, the rules of the menu and what each assumes, multiple imputation and a sensitivity band.
- [Bayesian estimation](bayesian.qmd) – the model of the claim as a posterior distribution: priors for the two-way design, persistent errors within a country, partial pooling of the country slopes and sensitivity to the priors.
- [Meta-analysis](meta-analysis.qmd) – the common scale of Multi100, the five analysts of the case on it, the two-way slope as a weighted average of the country slopes, and other studies of many analysts.
- [The multiverse and its critics](multiverse.qmd) – where multiverse analysis came from, the debate of 2025–26, robustness against replicability, and the curve of the case with its pruned menu and its displays of heterogeneity.

The reading on [the specification curve](../cases/eu-frames/reading-inference.qmd) of the case, on what a test of the curve as a whole can and cannot establish, belongs with these modules without being one of them.
